result.topic_en: The page argues that a definite binary form can be deformed into any other definite form without passing through forms with real zeros, proposes extending Noether's fundamental theorem to systems of forms, and restates Hilbert's theorem that not every definite form is a sum of squares, phrased as a mapping problem.

items.english: State my theorem on the impossibility of representing definite forms as sums of squares as follows: it is not possible, by means of a real rational quadratic transformation, to map the field of definite forms onto the infinite space of arbitrarily high dimension.
